hints: Factor out $-2$ from the terms involving $x$ before completing the square.
walkthrough:
Complete the square inside the bracket:
$$f(x) = 7 - 2\left[ (x + 3)^2 - 9 \right] = 7 - 2(x + 3)^2 + 18 = 25 - 2(x + 3)^2$$

hints: Use your completed-square form: the stationary point occurs when its squared term is zero.
walkthrough:
State the stationary point from the completed square form $y = 25 - 2(x + 3)^2$:
$$\text{Stationary Point: } (-3, \, 25)$$

State the minimum value of $k$ from the $x$-coordinate of the vertex for $g$ to be one-to-one:
$$k = -3$$

Set $y = 25 - 2(x + 3)^2$ and make $(x + 3)^2$ the subject:
$$2(x + 3)^2 = 25 - y \implies (x + 3)^2 = \frac{25 - y}{2}$$

Take the square root, choosing the positive root since $x \ge -3$:
$$x + 3 = \sqrt{\frac{25 - y}{2}} \implies x = \sqrt{\frac{25 - y}{2}} - 3$$

Express the inverse function in terms of $x$:
$$g^{-1}(x) = \sqrt{\frac{25 - x}{2}} - 3$$
